Rashi on Nazir 20a:1:1.hebrew: וב"ה סברי משום אוירא גזרו - וחמירא טומאתה, ומשום הכי צריכה דתיהוי כבתחלה:
Rashi on Nazir 20a:1:1.english: And Beit Hillel hold they decreed because of its airspace - And its impurity is severe, and on that account it is necessary that [the naziriteship] be from the beginning.

Rashi on Nazir 20a:1:2.hebrew: לא דכ"ע משום גושה גזרו - דקילא טומאה, והאי דאמרו לה דתיהדר לנזירותה — קנסא בעלמא הוא דקנסוה:
Rashi on Nazir 20a:1:2.english: No, everyone [agrees that] they decreed because of its earth - For [its] ritual impurity is lenient; and that which they said to her, that she must return to her naziriteship — it was merely a penalty that they penalized her.

Rashi on Nazir 20a:2:1.hebrew: איבעיא להו - הא דא"ר יהודה, דלא היתה נזירה אלא י"ד — בשנטמאת קאמר:
Rashi on Nazir 20a:2:1.english: A dilemma was raised before them - That which Rabbi Yehuda said, that she was a nazirite for only fourteen [years] — was he speaking of [a case] where she became impure?

Rashi on Nazir 20a:2:2.hebrew: ואליבא דב"ש - דכשעלתה לארץ, והיתה עושה ל' יום כב"ש, נטמאת בטומאת מת, וסתרה את הכל, ועשתה ז' שנים אחרים כבתחלה:
Rashi on Nazir 20a:2:2.english: And in accordance with Beit Shammai - That when she went up to the Land [of Israel] and was observing thirty days in accordance with Beit Shammai, she became defiled with corpse impurity and forfeited everything, and observed another seven years from the beginning.

Rashi on Nazir 20a:2:3.hebrew: או דלמא שלא נטמאת - אלא בשביל שבאת בארץ העמים ועלתה לא"י, עשתה ז' שנים כבתחלה, ואליבא דב"ה:
Rashi on Nazir 20a:2:3.english: Or perhaps that she did not become impure - Rather, [only] because she had been in the land of the nations and ascended to the Land of Israel, she observed seven years anew, and [this is] in accordance with Beit Hillel.

Rashi on Nazir 20a:3:1.hebrew: ת"ש עלתה לארץ ואי ס"ד כו' - ואי ס"ד כשנטמאת ואליבא דב"ש, אי הכי, ״י"ד שנה ול' יום״ מיבעיא ליה! שהרי בתוך ל' נטמאת, וסתרה כל שלמפרע — ז' שנה ול' יום — א"כ, ז' שנים ול' יום היה לה למנות תחתיהן. אלא מדלא תני הכי, אלא ״י"ד שנה״, ש"מ דבלא נטמאת מיירי ר' יהודה, ואליבא דב"ה. ע"א: איבעיא להו, הא דא"ר יהודה ״לא היתה נזירה אלא י"ד שנה״ — כשנטמאת עוד טומאה אחרת בסוף שבעה ראשונים, אבל לא יום מלאת, ועדיין יש לה יום אחד או ב' מן הז' שנים, ולבסוף ז' שנים עלתה לארץ ומנתה ז' שנים אחרות, שהרי סותרת ז' שנים ראשונים לד"ה, דהא נטמאת — הרי י"ד שנה; ולהכי לא אמרי ב"ש דצריכה למנות ל' יום בארץ, דהא סגי לה באותן ז' שנים שהיא מונה בארץ. תא שמע: ״עלתה לארץ כו'״, ואי ס"ד כשנטמאת ואליבא דב"ש, דנטמאת בסוף ז' ראשונים וחזרה ונטמאת בסוף י"ד כדאמר ת"ק — אי הכי, ״י"ד שנה ול' יום״ איבעי ליה לרבי יהודה למימר! דכיון שנטמאת בסוף י"ד, דיום מלאת, היתה צריכה למנות עוד ל', דהא ס"ל דכי נטמאת ביום מלאת מונה ל'. תניא נמי הכי, דלר' יהודה אית ליה דכי נטמאת ביום מלאת מונה ל'. וכיון דס"ל הכי, ודאי הא דא"ר יהודה ״לא היתה נזירה אלא י"ד שנה״ — בשלא נטמאת; וקא פליג אתנא קמא, דסבירא ליה לרבי יהודה דלא נטמאת כלל, אלא לסוף שבע שנים עלתה לארץ, והורוה שתהא נזירה עוד שבע שנים. ובלשון הזה דן ר"א ב"ר יצחק הלוי לפני רבינו, וקבלה (כ"ל ז"ה גליו"ן):
Rashi on Nazir 20a:3:1.english:
Come and hear: She ascended to the Land... And if it enters your mind, etc. - And if it enters your mind [that Rabbi Yehuda said this in a case] where she became ritually impure, and in accordance with [the opinion of] Beit Shammai — if so, he should have said: "Fourteen years and thirty days!" For she became impure within the thirty [days in Eretz Yisrael], and forfeited all that was retroactive — seven years and thirty days; if so, she should have counted seven years and thirty days in their place! Rather, since he does not teach this, but rather "fourteen years," conclude from this that Rabbi Yehuda is speaking of [a case where] she did not become impure, and in accordance with [the opinion of] Beit Hillel.

Another explanation: The dilemma was raised before them [as follows]: That which Rabbi Yehuda said, "She was a nazirite for only fourteen years," [was this] in a case where she contracted another [corpse] impurity at the end of the first seven [years], but not on the day of completion — rather, she still had one or two days left of the seven years — and at the end of seven years she ascended to the Land and counted another seven years, for she forfeits the first seven years according to all opinions, since she became impure; behold fourteen years! And therefore Beit Shammai did not say that she needs to count thirty days in the Land, for those seven years that she counts in the Land are sufficient for her.

[And the Gemara answers:] Come and hear: "She ascended to the Land, etc." And if it enters your mind [that he said this in a case] where she became impure, and in accordance with [the opinion of] Beit Shammai, [namely] that she became impure at the end of the first seven [years] and then became impure again at the end of the fourteen [years], as the First Tanna said — if so, Rabbi Yehuda should have said: "Fourteen years and thirty days!" For since she became impure at the end of the fourteen [years], which was the day of completion, she needed to count another thirty [days], for he holds that when one becomes impure on the day of completion, one counts thirty [days]. It is also taught thus [in a baraita]: that Rabbi Yehuda holds that when one becomes impure on the day of completion, one counts thirty [days]. And since he holds this, certainly that which Rabbi Yehuda said, "She was a nazirite for only fourteen years," was in a case where she did not become impure; and he disagrees with the First Tanna, for Rabbi Yehuda holds that she did not become impure at all, but rather at the end of seven years she ascended to the Land, and they instructed her that she should be a nazirite for another seven years.

And in this formulation, Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Yitzchak HaLevi argued before Rabbeinu, and he accepted it. (All this is a marginal gloss.)

Rashi on Nazir 20a:6:1.hebrew: כת אחת - אחד אומר שתי שנים קיבל עליו נזירות, ואחד אומר חמש שנים:
Rashi on Nazir 20a:6:1.english: One set - One [witness] says: He accepted upon himself two years of naziriteship, and one says: Five years.

Rashi on Nazir 20a:6:2.hebrew: שב"ש אומרים נחלקה העדות - הואיל ואין שם ב' עדים על ב' שנים:
Rashi on Nazir 20a:6:2.english: That Beit Shammai say: The testimony is divided - Since there are not two witnesses [testifying] to two years.

Rashi on Nazir 20a:6:3.hebrew: וב"ה אומרים - מ"מ שניהם מעידים על ב' שנים, ויש בכלל חמש שתים, ולא נחלקה עדותן. אבל בשני כיתי עדים — אחת אומרת שתים ואחת אומרת חמש — דברי הכל יש בכלל חמש שתים:
Rashi on Nazir 20a:6:3.english: And Beit Hillel say - In any case, both of them testify to two years, and two are included within five, and their testimony is not divided. But in [the case of] two sets of witnesses, [where] one says two and one says five, all agree that two are included within five.

Rashi on Nazir 20a:7:1.english: Rav said: All agree in [a case of] counting - That their testimony is divided.

Rashi on Nazir 20a:7:2.hebrew: מאי קאמר אילימא באחד אומר חמש ולא שתים ואחד אומר שתים ולא חמש - פשיטא דנחלקה עדותן, דהא קא מכחשי אהדדי:
Rashi on Nazir 20a:7:2.english: What is he saying? If we say in [a case where] one says five and not two, and one says two and not five - It is obvious that their testimony is divided, for they contradict each other:

Rashi on Nazir 20a:7:3.hebrew: אלא - כגון שהאחד אומר: אחת, שתים, והאחד אומר: שלש, ארבע, חמש:
Rashi on Nazir 20a:7:3.english: Rather - For example, where one [witness] says: "One, two," and the other says: "Three, four, five."

Tosafot on Nazir 20a:1:1.hebrew: לימא בהא קמיפלגי דב"ש סברי ארץ העמים משום גושא גזרו וב"ה סברי משום אוירא גזרו - אית ספרים דגרסי הכי: דב"ש סברי ארץ העמים משום גושא גזרו עליה ולא על אוירא, ומותר ליכנס בה בשידה, תיבה ומגדל; וב"ה סברי: אפילו על אוירא גזרו, ומש"ה החמירו לסתור הכל. וקשה לגירסא זו: דמאי טעמא דב"ש? דנהי דלא גזרו כי אם משום גושא, מ"מ לסתור הכל, מידי דהוה אבית הקברות דאינו מטמא באויר, ואפ"ה סותר הכל! לכן נראה דגרסינן איפכא: ב"ש סברי משום אוירא גזרו, והחמירו בארץ העמים, וב"ה סברי משום גושא גזרו. וא"ת: והשתא נמי, מאי טעמא דב"ש? אטו משום דהחמירו בה יותר מקבר לא יסתור אלא ל'? וי"ל: דאין הכי נמי, דכיון דהחמירו בה לגזור על אוירא, גלוי לכל דאותה טומאה אינה אלא מדרבנן, ולכך סגי לן דיסתור שלשים יום, דלא מיחלפא בטומאה דאורייתא; וב"ה סברי: משום גושא גזרו, וכיון דדינה כקבר צריך שיסתור הכל, ומשום דמיחלפא ארץ העמים בקברות. וכענין סברא זו איכא בפ' כהן גדול (לקמן נזיר דף נד:) דקאמר: אי משום אוירא, ל"ל הזאה? אבל אי משום גושא, ניחא, דטעמא דהזאה כשאר טומאות. ולפ"ז ה"ג: לא, דכ"ע משום אוירא גזרו, ולכך ניחא לב"ש דלא קניס אלא ל' יום, וב"ה סברי: אע"ג דגלוי לכל דטומאה דרבנן הוא ואינה כשאר אהל, קנסינן ליה בתחילת נזירות, ובקנסא הוא דפליגי:
Tosafot on Nazir 20a:1:1.english: "Let us say that they disagree about this: Beit Shammai hold that with regard to the land of the nations, they decreed on its earth, and Beit Hillel hold that they decreed on its airspace" - There are texts that read this as follows: Beit Shammai hold that with regard to the land of the nations, they decreed upon its earth and not upon its airspace, and it is permitted to enter it in a carriage, a chest, or a turret; and Beit Hillel hold that they decreed even upon its airspace, and for that reason they were stringent [requiring him] to negate everything. And this reading is difficult: For what is Beit Shammai's reasoning? For granted that they decreed only because of its earth, nevertheless let him negate everything, just as is the case with a cemetery, which does not impart impurity in [its] airspace, and even so negates everything! Therefore, it appears that we should read the reverse: Beit Shammai hold that they decreed because of its airspace, and were stringent regarding the land of the nations; and Beit Hillel hold that they decreed because of its earth. And if you say: Now too, what is Beit Shammai's reasoning? Is it because they were more stringent regarding it than regarding a grave that he should negate only thirty [days]? And one can say: Indeed so! For since they were stringent regarding it to decree upon its airspace, it is evident to all that this impurity is only rabbinic; therefore, it is sufficient for us that he negate thirty days, so that it will not be confused with Torah impurity. And Beit Hillel hold that they decreed because of its earth, and since its legal status is like a grave, he must negate everything, because the land of the nations is [liable to be] confused with cemeteries. And an idea similar to this reasoning is found in the chapter [entitled] Kohen Gadol (below, Nazir 54b), where [the Gemara] says: If [the decree was] because of its airspace, why do I need sprinkling? But if it was because of its earth, it is understandable, as the reason for sprinkling is like other impurities. And according to this, this is the version to read: 'No, everyone agrees that they decreed because of its airspace.' And therefore it works out well according to Beit Shammai that they penalized [him] only thirty days; and Beit Hillel hold that even though it is evident to all that it is a rabbinic impurity and is not like another tent, we penalize him [to start] at the beginning of naziriteship; and it is regarding the penalty that they disagree.

Tosafot on Nazir 20a:2:1.hebrew: בשנטמאת ואליבא דב"ש - [אמר] רבי יהודה, דהוצרכה למנות ל' יום בא"י, ונטמאה בסוף ל' יום בא"י, ומנתה עוד ז' שנים, שהרי הוצרכה לסתור כל נזירות; ונמצא דלר' יהודה היתה י"ד שנים ול' יום. והיינו דוקא לב"ש, דאין צריך למנות בא"י רק ל' יום לבד; דאי לב"ה, זקוקה לחזור ולמנות בא"י ז' שנים אחרים. אי נטמאת בסוף מנין כנטמאת דלעיל, היה כך: שנטמאה בסוף מנין של הארץ, וא"כ היתה צריכה להא נזירות כ"א שנה. או דלמא בשלא נטמאת, ודר' יהודה אליבא דב"ה דוקא; דלב"ש לא הוצרכה לי"ד שנים, ובז' שנים ול' יום סגי:
Tosafot on Nazir 20a:2:1.english: "Where she became impure, and in accordance with Beit Shammai" - [Did] Rabbi Yehuda [say that she was a nazirite for only fourteen years because] she was required to observe thirty days in Eretz Yisrael, and she became impure at the end of the thirty days in Eretz Yisrael, and observed another seven years, since she was required to forfeit the entire naziriteship; and [thus] it turns out that according to Rabbi Yehuda, it was fourteen years and thirty days? And this is specifically according to Beit Shammai, who [hold that] one needs to observe in Eretz Yisrael only thirty days alone; for according to Beit Hillel, she would be required to return and observe another seven years in Eretz Yisrael. If she became impure at the end of [her] count, like [the case of] her becoming impure mentioned earlier [in the Mishnah], it would be such that she became impure at the end of the count of the Land, and if so, she would have needed twenty-one years for this naziriteship. Or perhaps [the dilemma is whether Rabbi Yehuda speaks of a case] where she did not become impure, and Rabbi Yehuda's [statement] is specifically in accordance with Beit Hillel; for according to Beit Shammai, she would not have needed fourteen years, and seven years and thirty days would have sufficed.

Tosafot on Nazir 20a:3:1.hebrew: תא שמע עלתה לא"י וכו' ואי ס"ד בנטמאת ואליבא דב"ש אי הכי ר' יהודה אומר לא היתה נזירה אלא י"ד שנה י"ד שנה ול' יום מיבעי ליה - ולא גרסינן מה שכתוב בספרים: "ועוד מתניתין". וא"ת: ודלמא ל' יום היו מובלעים בז' שנים הראשונים — כגון שעשתה בחו"ל ז' שנים חסר חדש, ושלשים יום דקנסא בארץ, [הרי] ז' שנים ולא יותר; ונטמאה בסוף ל' יום של הקנס, ועשתה עוד ז' שנים, הרי י"ד בין הכל? ועוד קשה: למה לו להאריך דברי ת"ק? לא יביא אלא דברי ר' יהודה לדקדק מהם! וי"ל: דמש"ה מייתי דברי ת"ק, לאוכוחי דלת"ק לא מיירי בהבלעה — דקתני: "ולבסוף שבע שנים נטמאת ונמצאת נזירה כ"א שנה (ול' יום)"; [א"כ] גם דברי ר' יהודה לא מיירי בהבלעה, וא"כ י"ד שנים ושלשים יום מיבעי ליה:
Tosafot on Nazir 20a:3:1.english: “Come and hear: She ascended to Eretz [Yisrael], etc. And if it enters your mind [that the case is one] where she became ritually impure, and in accordance with Beit Shammai — if so, [why does] Rabbi Yehuda say: ‘She was a nazirite for only fourteen years’? He should have [said]: ‘Fourteen years and thirty days’!” - And we do not maintain the textual reading found in [some] books: “And furthermore, the mishna [teaches].” And if you will say: But perhaps the thirty days were subsumed within the first seven years — such as where she observed seven years minus a month outside of Eretz [Yisrael], and the thirty days of the penalty [were observed] in Eretz [Yisrael], [which makes] seven years and no more; and she became ritually impure at the end of the thirty days of the penalty, and observed another seven years, behold, [there are] fourteen [years] in all? And furthermore, it is difficult: Why did [the Gemara] need to quote at length the words of the First Tanna? It should have brought only the words of Rabbi Yehuda to deduce [its proof] from them! And one can say: That is why it brings the words of the First Tanna, to prove that according to the First Tanna, [the mishna] is not dealing with subsumption — as it teaches: “And at the end of seven years she became ritually impure, and she was found to be a nazirite for twenty-one years (and thirty days)”; [if so,] Rabbi Yehuda’s words are also not dealing with subsumption, and if so, he should have [said]: “Fourteen years and thirty days.”

Tosafot on Nazir 20a:5:1.hebrew: מי שהיו שתי כתי עדים מעידות אותו אלו מעידין שנדר שני נזירות ואלו מעידין שנדר חמש נחלקה עדותן - ואין כאן נזירות כלל. וא"ת: היכי דמי? אם שתק הנודר — שתיקה כהודאה דמיא! וי"ל: שהנודר מכחיש כל אחת ואחת; דאי מודה לאחת, למה לא יהיה כהודאתו? א"נ, באומר: "איני יודע", והשתא צריך לידון לפי העדות. א"נ, כששותק ובאו שתי הכיתות יחד, דלא הוי שתיקותיה כהודאה — דלאו מודה הוא, דאמר: מה לי להכחישן, הא שתיהן מכחישין זה את זה! וב"ה אומרים: "יש בכלל חמש שתים" — [ומונה] ב', דהוי כאילו אמרו שתיהן: "שתים נדרת":
Tosafot on Nazir 20a:5:1.english: "One who had two sets of witnesses testifying about him: these testify that he vowed two terms of naziriteship, and these testify that he vowed five; their testimony is divided" - And there is no naziriteship here at all. And if you say: What are the circumstances? If the one who vowed was silent, silence is considered like an admission! And one can say: That the one who vowed contradicts each and every [set]; for if he admits to one, why would it not be according to his admission? Alternatively, [it is a case] where he says: "I do not know," and now it is necessary to judge according to the testimony. Alternatively, when he remains silent and both sets came together, so that his silence is not considered like an admission — for he does not admit, since he says: "Why should I contradict them? Behold, both of them contradict each other!" And Beit Hillel say: "Two are included in five" — [and he counts] two, for it is as though both [sets] said: "You vowed two."

Tosafot on Nazir 20a:6:1.hebrew: מתניתין - דקתני דפליגי ב"ש וב"ה בשתי כתי עדות, [דלא כהאי] תנא דר' ישמעאל:
Tosafot on Nazir 20a:6:1.english: "The Mishnah" - Which teaches that Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel disagree with regard to two sets of witnesses, [is not in accordance with this] tanna of Rabbi Yishmael.

Tosafot on Nazir 20a:7:1.hebrew: אמר רב הכל מודים במונה - שנחלקה העדות. לרבי ישמעאל, דאמר דפליגי בית שמאי ובית הלל בכת אחת — היינו כשאומר אחד שתים ואחד אומר חמש; אבל אם מונה, כדמסיק ואזיל — נחלקה העדות:
Tosafot on Nazir 20a:7:1.english: Rav said: All concede in a case of counting - That the testimony is divided. According to Rabbi Yishmael, who said that Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel disagree with regard to a single set [of witnesses] — that is when one [witness] says "two" and one says "five"; but if [one] counts, as [the Gemara] proceeds to conclude, the testimony is divided.

Tosafot on Nazir 20a:7:2.hebrew: מאי קאמר - כלומר, והיכי דמי "מונה" דקאמר? אילימא דקא מכחשי אהדדי להדיא, כדקאמר "חמש ולא שתים" כו' — פשיטא דנחלקה עדותן, ומאי קא משמע לן רב? אלא, אחד אומר "אחת ושתים" ואחד אומר "שלש וארבע וחמש", ואינם מכחישים בפירוש זה את זה; וקמ"ל רב, דכיון דכל חד וחד נחת למניינא — שזה אינו אומר "שתים" בבת אחת אלא אומר "אחת ושתים", וזה "ג' וארבע וה'" ולא "אחת ושתים" — כאילו אמר: "לא אחת ושתים נדר, אלא של שלש וארבע וה'", וזה שאמר "אחת ושתים" כאילו אומר: "ולא נדר שלש וארבע וחמש":
Tosafot on Nazir 20a:7:2.english: What is he saying - That is to say: And what is the case of "counting" that [Rav] is speaking of? If we say that they explicitly contradict each other, as when [the Gemara] says, "Five and not two," etc. — it is obvious that their testimony is divided, and what is Rav teaching us? Rather, [it is a case where] one [witness] says "one and two," and one says "three, four, and five," and they do not explicitly contradict one another. And Rav teaches us that since each and every one entered into a count — for this one does not say "two" all at once, but rather says "one and two," and that one [says] "three, four, and five," and not "one and two" — it is as though he said: "He did not vow one and two, but rather [a vow] of three, four, and five"; and this one who said "one and two" is as though he says: "And he did not vow three, four, and five."
